title: 4 Programmatic Advertising Mistakes to Avoid This BFCM and Holiday Season
summary: Avoid four common BFCM advertising mistakes that could cost your brand valuable opportunities, from overlooked audiences and outdated targeting to missed moments of consumer intent.
body_markdown:
Adobe forecasts[$275.1 billion in U.S. online holiday spending in 2026](https://news.adobe.com/news/2026/09/adobe-us-holiday-shopping-season-to-hit-record?_bhlid=e056cd7e0293bdb634e3e312f758f81b32c35ca5&utm_source=chatgpt.com) , up 6.7% year over year, with Cyber Week alone expected to generate $47.5 billion. With Black Friday and Cyber Monday (BFCM) fast approaching, most advertisers already have their holiday campaigns in motion. But even the best-laid plans can leave opportunities on the table. Here are four common programmatic advertising mistakes to avoid as the holiday shopping season ramps up.


## **Mistake #1: Relying on Just One Advertising Channel**


Your customers aren’t confined to one screen. Your advertising shouldn’t be either.


Holiday shoppers discover products on connected TV (CTV), compare options on mobile, and encounter brand messaging across display, online video, and other channels. Concentrating spend in one environment limits opportunities to reach consumers throughout that journey.


CTV deserves particular attention. According to


[EMARKETER](https://www.emarketer.com/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) , U.S. **CTV advertising spending is expected to surpass traditional linear TV advertising in 2027** , reflecting the continued shift toward streaming.


Advances in audience intelligence also make CTV targeting more adaptable. Inuvo’s IntentKey, for example, uses[short-lived neighborhood-level models](https://inuvo.com/intentkey-takes-identity-free-ctv-targeting-to-the-neighborhood-level/) to identify local interests without building persistent profiles of individuals or households.


**The takeaway:** Diversify your media mix across CTV, online video, display, and streaming audio to reach consumers in different environments and mindsets, creating more opportunities to engage them at the right moment in their purchase journey.


## **Mistake #2: Running One Message for Each Audience**


One product can attract dozens of audiences. Even within those audiences, the motivations behind a purchase vary.


Consider a premium coffee maker. One shopper values convenience. Another enjoys the craft. A third is searching for the perfect holiday gift.


Same product. Three different reasons to buy.


Traditional audience segmentation misses these distinctions. Concept-based audience intelligence helps advertisers understand the interests, ideas, and motivations connected to a product by analyzing patterns in online content consumption.


Those connections are extracted by IntentKey as insights to inform creative that speaks to what consumers actually care about, rather than relying on a single message for everyone.


**The takeaway:** Build creative variations around different purchase motivations. Test messaging that emphasizes convenience, value, gifting, or lifestyle depending on the interests shaping each audience.


## **Mistake #3: Looking for New Customers in Your Old Customer Data**


Your next customer doesn’t have to look like your last.


Historical purchase data, remarketing, and lookalike audiences remain valuable tools, but all rely on identity. Relying exclusively on them keeps prospecting tied to people who have already purchased or resemble existing customers.


That leaves emerging interests and unexpected purchase motivations outside the picture.


Intent-based audience discovery expands prospecting by identifying the concepts connecting consumers to products and categories, without requiring a customer list or predefined demographic profile.


For example, **Inuvo’s**


**[James & James furniture case study](https://inuvo.com/success-stories/james-and-james/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)** demonstrates how exploring interests beyond conventional furniture audiences helped uncover new opportunities for targeting and messaging.


**The takeaway:** Dedicate part of your holiday strategy to net-new audience discovery. Explore interests adjacent to your products instead of limiting prospecting to historical customer profiles.


## **Mistake #4: Making Decisions With Yesterday’s Audience Signals**


Holiday demand moves quickly. Audience targeting needs to keep pace.


A shopper researching electronics today could be comparing kitchen appliances tomorrow. Static segments and historical behavior alone cannot capture every change in consumer interest as it develops.


Real-time audience intelligence gives advertisers a more current view of the concepts and interests shaping demand.


**IntentKey** analyzes **open-web content consumption patterns** and refreshes its audience models every **five minutes** . Its predictive intelligence also provides visibility into emerging audience size and sentiment trends, helping advertisers identify changes in demand **up to 24 hours ahead.**


****


The value extends beyond targeting. These signals help inform creative decisions, audience discovery, and campaign optimizations throughout the shopping season.


**The takeaway:** Rethink how you approach BFCM and your broader programmatic strategy. Prioritize real-time audience intelligence over historical assumptions to identify emerging demand, uncover new opportunities, and reach consumers while their interest is forming.


## **The Holiday Shopping Season Isn’t Over. Neither Is the Opportunity.**


Black Friday is approaching, but consumer demand will continue well beyond Cyber Monday. Brands that diversify their reach, adapt creative to different motivations, discover new audiences, and respond to emerging intent will be better positioned to capture opportunities throughout the season.
